column1: # Functions that meet the "documented" stage (docs/PROGRESS.md): prototype, purpose, side effects and
# callers recorded here, applied to Ghidra by tools/ghidra/ApplySignatures.java, and described in the doc.
# Columns are tab-separated: address, C prototype, summary (purpose and side effects), document.

column3: summary
Builds the sorted disc file index from umd1: (PVD, path table, recursive directory walk). Side effects: allocates the pool, sets 0x089218c8/cc/d0/d4/d8, sorts, sets ready flag 0x089218dc.

column2: void container_index_directory(int fd, char *prefix, uint lba, int size)
column3: Appends one 16-byte index entry per file in an ISO 9660 directory and recurses into subdirectories. Side effects: advances 0x089218cc (entries) and 0x089218d0 (name pool).
Binary-searches the file index for path (without the disc0: prefix); returns the extent LBA or -1 and stores the size. No side effects.
Size of root-relative path: file index for disc paths, otherwise sceIoGetstat; -1 if missing. No side effects.

column2: int container_resolve_path(char *buf, int root, char *path, int no_lbn)
column3: Writes roots[root] + path into buf and, for indexed disc paths when no_lbn is 0, rewrites it as disc0:/sce_lbn0x%04x_size0x%04x. Returns 1. Side effects: buf only.
Non-zero when the path starts with the word "disc". No side effects.
Non-zero when the first three bytes are "EHP". No side effects.
Case-insensitive binary search of the EHP entry table; returns the (name offset, data offset) entry or 0. No side effects.
Member size: the unaligned u32 after the name for version 3, offset difference for older versions. No side effects.
Returns a pointer to the named member's data (0 if absent or not an EHP) and optionally its size. No side effects.
Binds an archive once: writes "BIND" over "NOT ", prepares members, then runs and clears the one-shot callback at 0x08921918. Returns 0 if flag is negative, else 1.

Prepares each member in place by extension (ptrs.txt resource lists turned into pointers, .tmt/.tma/.tms/.ehf/.gim handlers, runtime handler table). Returns 1. Side effects: member data, handler state.
If cardinfo is loaded: clears 0x1e2c bytes at 0x08924d1c, binds the archive and stores pointers to its 14 members in the globals there. Returns the loaded flag.
Record index of a card id via CARD_IntID; 0 for ids below 0xe88. No side effects.
Pointer to the card's UTF-16 name in CARD_Name. No side effects.
Pointer to the card's 8-byte CARD_Prop record. No side effects.
The card's passcode from CARD_Pass. No side effects.
Decodes and expands the card's description into the next of four rotating 0x77a-byte buffers at 0x08924d5c and returns it. Side effects: rotation counter 0x08926b44, that buffer.
Huffman-decodes one description with the CARD_Huff tree into out until the zero symbol; returns out. Side effects: out only.
Copies in to out, replacing $d + three characters with dictionary words; returns out. Side effects: out only.
Returns dictionary word number; when it contains %c + four digits, expands card names into the next of 50 rotating 0x200-byte buffers at 0x08ac6580. 0 when out of range.
Status from the built-in limit list (0 forbidden, 1 limited, 2 semi-limited) or 3 when unlisted. No side effects.
Sets every card id 0xe88-0x1f39 to unlimited, then applies the 114 built-in limit entries, via deck_set_limit.
C strcpy. Side effects: dst.
C strcat. Side effects: dst.
C strlen. No side effects.
C strcasecmp using the ctype table at 0x088779c9. No side effects.

column2: void * system_bsearch(void *key, void *base, uint count, uint size, void *compare)
column3: C bsearch; returns the matching element or 0. No side effects.
1 when buf starts with the gzip magic 1F 8B. No side effects.

column2: int sceGzipDecompress(void *dst, uint dst_size, void *src, uint *crc32)
column3: Inflates a gzip stream into dst; returns the output size or an SCE error code and stores the trailer CRC-32. Side effects: dst, crc32.

Builds "cardinfo_" + language code + ".ehp" and queues its load from root 5 (duelsys) into 0x08926b50 with completion callback card_db_on_cardinfo_loaded. Side effects: clears the loaded flag 0x08926b48, sets 0x08926b4c.
File-thread completion callback of card_db_load_cardinfo: sets the loaded flag 0x08926b48 to 1 and returns 1 (accept the read).
Appends the upper-cased first letter of the current language code (table 0x08878c88) and the suffix string at 0x0889f8b0 to name. Side effects: name only.
Returns 0xffff when bit 0 of CARD_Prop word 1 (the odd card kind) is set, which holds for every real record, else 0 (record 0, unused ids). No side effects.
The card's position in the alphabetical list, CARD_Sort[index]. No side effects.
CARD_Prop word 1 bits 22-24 (meaning unknown; values 0, 1, 3, 4). Exported. No side effects.
Linear search of ids 0xe88-0x1f39 for the passcode; returns the card id or -1 (also for passcode 0). No side effects.
Pointer to UTF-16 DLG string number: DLG_Text + DLG_Indx[number]. No bounds check. No side effects.
Name of a monster type (race): DLG 500 + race, or the empty fallback string 0x088a711c for 0. No side effects.
Kind suffix ("/Effect", "/Fusion", ...): DLG 550 + kind after mapping tuner kinds 15/16 to 11, synchro 17 to 12, 18 to 13 and other kinds above 10 to 1; fallback string for kind 0. No side effects.
Attribute name: DLG 530 + attribute (1 LIGHT ... 9 TRAP), fallback string for 0. No side effects.
Spell/trap icon name: DLG 570 + icon (1 Counter ... 7 Normal), fallback string for 0. No side effects.
Monster type (race), CARD_Prop word 1 bits 17-21 (23 spell, 24 trap). No side effects.
Attribute, CARD_Prop word 1 bits 6-9. No side effects.
Level, CARD_Prop word 1 bits 10-13. No side effects.
Spell/trap icon, CARD_Prop word 1 bits 14-16. No side effects.
Card kind index, CARD_Prop word 1 bits 1-5 (stored kind >> 1: 0 normal, 1 effect, ... 10 token, 13 spell, 14 trap); ids 0x1386-0x1388 always return 11. No side effects.
ATK = 10 x CARD_Prop word 0 bits 14-22; the value 0x1ff ("?") returns 0. No side effects.
DEF = 10 x CARD_Prop word 0 bits 23-31; 0x1ff ("?") returns 0. No side effects.
Like card_db_get_atk but returns 0xffff for "?". No side effects.
Like card_db_get_def but returns -1 for "?". No side effects.
Non-zero when CARD_Genre bit genre is set: word genre >> 4, bit genre & 15 of the record's three u16. No side effects.
Genre name, DLG 701 + genre for 0 <= genre < 40, else the fallback string 0x088a711c. No side effects.
Copies the record's three CARD_Genre words to out[0..2]. Side effects: out.
card_db_has_genre(card_id, table[filter]) with the 35-entry u32 table at 0x0889f980. No side effects.
Number of CARD_Top entries (27). No side effects.
Character of CARD_Top entry n (0 when n > count). No side effects.
First card id of CARD_Top entry n (0 when n > count). No side effects.
Index of the CARD_Top letter group that contains the card: last n whose first card sorts at or before it. No side effects.
Number of artworks: binary search of CARD_SamePict by record index, n + 1 when listed, 1 otherwise, 0 if the table is missing. No side effects.
Copies in to out, replacing "$m" + four digits with the name of that card id (format 0x0889f978); other "$x" pairs are copied unchanged. Returns out. Side effects: out.
1 when card_db_get_kind is 10 (token). No side effects.
1 when the card's race is 24 (trap). No side effects.
1 when the .cip header held at reader+0xac has magic "CPJ\x1a". No side effects.
1 when the .cip header held at reader+0xac has magic "CPM\x1a". No side effects.

Finds the next pending slot (state 1) in the reader's slot table, picks a buffer, marks the slot 2 and queues container_read_async of its sectors with callback card_db_on_cip_slot_read. Returns 1 if a read was queued.

Read-completion callback: unmasks the buffer for CPJ files (XOR head, then LCG stream), stores the buffer pointer in the slot and queues the next slot; clears reader flag bit 1 when none is left. Returns 1.
Pointer to the reader's slot table, reader + 0xac + *(reader+0xc8): pairs (sector, state or buffer) ending in -1. No side effects.
Returns the next of the reader's rotating image buffers (base +0x94, count +0x98, index +0x9c, size spi x 0x800) and resets slots whose data lived in it. Side effects: index, slot table.
Writes status (0-3) into bits 0-1 of byte 2 of the card's save collection record; ignored for status >= 4 or cards without a record. Side effects: game state.
The save's limit status of the card (byte 2 bits 0-1 of its collection record); 3 (unlimited) when it has no record. No side effects.
Limit status for deck building: the built-in list (deck_get_default_limit) when the flag 0x08aa5688 is set or use_builtin is 1, else the save copy (deck_get_limit). No side effects.
deck_get_card_limit(0, card_id). Exported. No side effects.
Clears the 0x80-byte UTF-16 field at game state +0x16582 and copies up to 63 units of name into it. Called by deck_reset_limits. Side effects: game state.
Pointer to the limit-list name at game state +0x16582. No side effects.
Pointer to the 0xc0-byte card lists (counts, main, side, extra) of deck slot slot: game state + 0x4914 + 0x16c x slot. No side effects.
Copies the 0xc0-byte card lists of deck slot slot to out. Side effects: out.
Copies the 64-byte UTF-16 deck name of slot slot (game state + 0x48d4 + 0x16c x slot) to out and forces a terminating NUL. Side effects: out.
Copies 64 bytes of name into the deck name of slot slot and forces a terminating NUL. Side effects: game state.

Fills the 0xc0-byte deck struct from member RCP<recipe>.ydc of the embedded archive 0x088d77e0 (main, extra, side with limits 60/15/15); clears it if the member is missing or a count is too large. Side effects: deck.
UTF-16 name of a recipe from recipe_name_<l>.bin (letter from "jegfis" by language), or 0 when RCP<recipe>.ydc does not exist. Result in the dictionary word buffers.
Level of a recipe from the u16 table at 0x089143f0 for 0 <= recipe < 462, else 1. No side effects.
Number of recipes of an owner (bsearch of the 126 x 16-byte table at 0x08915f28, field +8), 0 if unknown. No side effects.
Recipe number first + n of an owner when 0 <= n < count, else -1. No side effects.

Variant index of an owner's deck for a stage from the 67 x 12-byte table at 0x08916730 (owner 8 stage 1 adds 1 when the character has 2000 points or more); -1, 0 or 1 for other character modes. No side effects.
deck_get_owner_recipe(owner, deck_select_owner_variant(owner, stage)). No side effects.
bsearch comparator of the owner table: *a - *b. No side effects.
Base of the in-memory game state that DATA0 mirrors: 0x08aa5794 + 4 x (u32 at 0x08ac18c0, a random 0-15 chosen at boot). No side effects.

Clears 0x1c0ec bytes of game state and builds a new game: language kept, system nickname (at most 8 units, "$" doubled) at +0xfd5c, starting deck from recipe 0 (cards added to the collection, name in slot 1), OpenPSID at +0x10, default options, default limits, version 0x30000 at +0.

Writes the default option bits of the settings block and default volumes (0x08841724) and a 12-word block from 0x0885c084. Callers system_init_game_globals, save_init_new_game. Side effects: game state.
Pointer to the card's 4-byte collection record at game state + 0x11ba4 + 4 x index; 0 for index 0 and for tokens. No side effects.
Copies owned: collection byte 1 bits 0-6 (0 without a record). No side effects.
Sets the copies owned (bits 0-6 of byte 1) and the state bits 1-2 of byte 0: 2 if the card already had copies, else 1 (count > 0) or 0. Side effects: game state.
add != 0: one more copy (max 99), state 0 becomes 1 (new); add == 0: one copy fewer (not below 0). Side effects: game state.
Sets the state bits 1-2 of collection byte 0 to 2 (owned, no longer new). Side effects: game state.
1 when the collection state (byte 0 bits 1-2) is 1. No side effects.
Collection state, byte 0 bits 1-2: 0 never obtained, 1 new, 2 owned. No side effects.
Bit 3 of collection byte 0 (0 without a record). No side effects.
Sets bit 3 of collection byte 0. Side effects: game state.
Pointer to the 0x2a-byte record of pack pack at game state + 0x16604 + 0x2a x pack, 0 for pack >= 48. No side effects.
Writes state into bits 0-2 of pack record byte 1 (keeping bit 2 if it was set). Side effects: game state.
Pack record byte 1 bits 0-2 (0 for an invalid pack). No side effects.
Pointer to the 20 u16 entries at pack record +2 (0 for an invalid pack). No side effects.

column2: void save_set_pack_entry(int pack, int n, ushort value)
column3: Stores value in entry n (< 20) of a pack record. Side effects: game state.
Entry n (< 20) of a pack record, 0 when out of range. No side effects.
For all 48 packs: byte 0 = 0xaa, entries cleared (0x28 bytes). Side effects: game state.
Pointer to the settings bytes at game state + 0xfe04. No side effects.
Language index, settings byte 0 bits 0-2 (0 J, 1 E, 2 G, 3 F, 4 I, 5 S, after the "jegfis" letters). No side effects.
Writes settings byte 0 bits 0-2, then calls 0x088373c8. Side effects: game state.
Sets or clears one of six option bits: options 0-2 settings byte 1 bits 5-7, options 3-5 byte 2 bits 0, 3, 4. Side effects: game state.
Reads the option bit written by save_set_option_flag; 0 for other options. No side effects.
u32 n at game state + 0xfdfc + 4n (meaning not established). No side effects.
Pointer to the 0x18-byte per-character records at game state + 0xfe0c. No side effects.
Pointer to the character's 0x18-byte record. No side effects.
Appends value to the character record's u16 list (count at +0, up to 10 entries at +2) unless already present. Side effects: game state.
The character's points, u16 at record +0x16. No side effects.
Sets the points clamped to 0-8000. Side effects: game state.
Adds delta to the points, clamped to 0-8000. Side effects: game state.
Character 2-142 with the most points (first one on ties). No side effects.

Starts a save-data session: allocates from heap a 0x200 work block, a buffer for msd_e.ehp, the 0x9d0-byte SceUtilitySavedataParam and the 0x20000 save buffer, and queues msd_e.ehp from root 6. Returns 0 (and frees) on failure, else 1.
Frees the four save-session blocks to their heap and clears the pointers 0x08acda04-0x08acda10.
Completion callback of save_open: sets 0x08acd9f0 and binds the loaded msd_e.ehp archive. Returns 1.
Returns the file name "msd_e.ehp" (0x088a15cc). No side effects.

column2: int container_load_file(int root, char *path, void *dest, int size, void *callback, void *arg)
column3: Queues a whole-file read: container_read_async(root, path, dest, 0, size, callback, arg). Returns 1.

column2: int container_read_async(int root, char *path, void *dest, int offset, int size, void *callback, void *arg)
column3: Claims the next of 32 0x60-byte request slots at 0x08920cb4 under semaphore 0x089218b8, fills it as type 0 (read) and signals the queue semaphore 0x089218bc. Returns 1.
sceGzipDecompress with the CRC discarded; returns the output size or an SCE error. Exported. Side effects: dst.
If the one-shot callback slot 0x08921918 is free, stores callback and runs container_ehp_bind(ehp, 1); returns 1 then, else 0 without binding.

Clears the 0xc1c-byte file-queue state at 0x08920cac, stores config[0] as the root path table, starts the file thread (priority 0x6f, 8 KiB stack) and creates "ehfile_sema" and "ehfile_queue". Returns 1.

File thread: waits on the queue semaphore, takes a request, runs it (type 0 container_read_file, type 1 system_load_module), passes the result to callback(arg, result) and repeats the operation until the callback returns non-zero; then frees the slot.
First busy request slot, scanning the 32-slot ring from the write index 0x089218b4; 0 if none. No side effects.

column2: int container_read_file(int root, char *path, void *dest, int offset, int size)
column3: Synchronous read of size bytes at offset: resolves the path; non-disc paths via sceIoOpen/Lseek/Read/Close, disc paths via container_read_disc_file. Returns bytes read, -1 if the open fails, -2 if the seek fails.

column2: int container_read_disc_file(char *path, void *dest, int offset, int size)
column3: Same as container_read_file for a resolved disc path, through the wrappers 0x0881e2c4 (open), 0x0881e448 (seek), 0x0881e378 (read). Returns bytes read, -1 or -2.
Clears the scene slot 0x08920be4, requests module name (or the static function when name is 0), creates and starts thread "ehscript" at the caller's priority + 1 and runs it once. Returns 1.
Scene thread state machine on 0x08920c3c (1 load, 2 start, 3 enter, 5 run/exit); wakes the main thread after every step.
Load callback of the scene thread: stores uid at slot+0x50 when positive; returns uid > 0.
Resumes the scene thread and sleeps until it wakes the caller, then suspends it again. Returns 1.
Stores the scene's start and end callbacks and argument at 0x08920c28/2c/30. Returns 1.
Copies basename plus the suffix at 0x0889ed84 into the requested-name buffer 0x08920be8. Returns 1.
Requests the "staticmodule" pseudo-scene with fn as its function; fn is dropped (0) when its first word is a MIPS j instruction. Returns 1.
Resolves root + path and calls sceKernelLoadModule(path, 0, 0); returns the module UID or an error.

column2: int system_queue_module_load(int root, char *path, void *callback, void *arg)
column3: Queues a type-1 request (module load) in the file-thread queue. Returns 1.
Clears the 0x1304-byte registry at 0x089235b4, replaces roots -1/-2 of the built-in table 0x0889f57c by root_a/root_b and registers it.
Adds each 16-byte descriptor (id, root, name, kind) not yet registered as a 76-byte entry, then sorts the registry by id. Returns 1 if an id was already present.
bsearch of the registry by id; entry or 0. No side effects.
system_module_load_ex(id, 0, 0, 0x089248b8, 0). Returns 1 for an unknown id, else 0.

column2: int system_module_load_ex(int id, int argsize, void *argp, int *status, void *option)
column3: Increments the reference count and, when not loaded, queues the load (kind 0) with start arguments or loads a utility module (kind 4). Returns 1 for an unknown id, else 0.
Load callback: stores uid, sceKernelStartModule with the saved arguments, state 2. Returns uid > 0.
0 while any registry entry is in state 1 (loading), else 1. No side effects.
Decrements the reference count of a loaded module and stops/unloads it at 0. Returns 1 for an unknown id or a module still loading, else 0.
Module file name without its 4-character extension, copied to 0x089248c0; 0 for an unknown id.
Module file name copied to 0x089248e0; 0 for an unknown id.
system_module_load of ids 2-5 (video playback). Returns 0.
system_module_unload of ids 5-2. Returns 0.

Loads module ids 3, 7, 6 and waits for them, creates the 0x280000-byte heap at 0x08acda40, installs three callbacks (0x088414a0, 0x08841514, 0x08841554) through 0x08869290 and calls 0x08841724(n, 12) for n = 0-2.
Loads and starts libfont.prx, opens the default font (and an optimum 20 x 20 font when alt_font), stores its metrics and sets the alternative character 0x25a1. Returns 1.
Module base name of a scene id through the 31-entry table 0x088a1478 (sorted on first use); "unknown id" otherwise.

column2: void system_scene_call(int from, int to, int arg)
column3: Pushes transition {1, from, to, arg} on the scene stack and requests to's module.
Sets the current transition to {2, from, caller, arg}, pops the stack and requests the caller's module.

column2: void system_scene_jump(int from, int to, int arg)
column3: Clears the scene stack, sets {3, from, to, arg} and requests to's module.
from of the top stack entry when its to is scene, else 31. No side effects.
Copies the current 8-byte transition to out. Side effects: out.
Returns the 144-byte scene stack at 0x08aa56a4. No side effects.
Comparator of the scene table: *b - *a. No side effects.
Comparator of the module registry: *b - *a. No side effects.

Boot sequence and main loop: callbacks, UMD activation, file index, file thread, module registries, audio, game globals, font, scene "rel_title"; then per frame rand step, scene slice and housekeeping. Never returns.

column2: int system_exit_callback(int arg1, int arg2, void *common)
column3: Exit callback ("EXIT_CALLBACK"): calls 0x0882b8c0, then sceKernelExitGame. Returns 0.

column2: int system_power_callback(int unknown, int power_flags, void *common)
column3: Power callback ("POWER_CALLBACK"): stores power_flags at 0x08ac24bc. Returns 0.
When the pad state from 0x088284b8 (+0x24) holds SELECT+START+L+R (0x309) and 0x0881dd48 and 0x08835aac both return 0, reboots with sceKernelLoadExec("disc0:/PSP_GAME/SYSDIR/BOOT.BIN").

Binds the six embedded EHP archives, clears 0x1cefc bytes at 0x08aa5680, creates a 16 KiB heap, seeds rand, picks the random game-state offset 0x08ac18c0, finds loading.ehf and writes default options.
system_rand() >> 4. No side effects beyond the generator.
newlib reentrancy struct: the one at *(k0+4) when the thread has one, else the global at 0x0889e5b0. No side effects.
C strncpy (pads with NUL up to n). Returns dst. Side effects: dst.
strncpy for UTF-16: copies up to n units and pads with 0. Returns dst. Side effects: dst.
C sprintf through system_vfprintf_r with a string FILE of unlimited size; NUL-terminates buf.

column2: void system_qsort(void *base, uint count, uint size, void *compare)
column3: C qsort (BSD-style median-of-three quicksort with insertion sort below 7 elements). Side effects: base.
C malloc: system_malloc_r(system_get_reent(), size).
C free: system_free_r(system_get_reent(), ptr).
Initialises a "HOGE" (0x45474f48) heap header with its block list inside memory (when memory is 0, allocates a 16-byte header through 0x0880d1a0 instead). Returns the heap or 0.
Allocates size bytes rounded up to 16 from a HOGE heap (tail call to 0x08826458 with flag 1); 0 on failure or size < 1.
Marks the block of ptr free (header bit 31), bumps the heap's free counter and relinks the block through 0x08826fb8 (twice) and 0x088270ac. Returns 1.
bsearch of the 174 x 148-byte character records at 0x088aa510 by (u8 character, s8 variant); record or 0. No side effects.
Comparator of the character records: by u8 character, then signed u8 variant. No side effects.
1 when world_find_character finds a record. No side effects.
First bank of the character's voice set (record +0x30); 0 for characters 0 and 1. No side effects.
First of the four small voice banks (record +0x34) when the record has a voice set, else 0; 0 for characters 0 and 1. No side effects.
Global sound id of the bank's first cue: first[bank] through *(*0x08dd3004 + 0x20). No side effects.
Once per TMT ("TGMT", flag bit 0 at +0x34): turns the six section offsets into pointers and the per-entry data offsets into addresses. Returns tmt, or 0 when it is not a TGMT.
Once per TMA ("TGMA", flag at +0x20): turns three section offsets and the entry data offsets into pointers. Returns tma, or 0 when the magic differs.

Once per TMS ("TGMS", flag at +0x5c): relocates its sections, links each object's four sub-entries to their 0x28-byte records, replaces sub-entry type codes 2/1 by the functions 0x0882f050/0x0882ef50 and passes each record name through the hook 0x08924b14. Returns tms or 0.
Clears words +8 and +0xc of a GIM member at bind time. Side effects: gim.
Sets ctx+0x14 to a TGMT: used in place, or gunzipped into one of two alternating buffers and bound; 0 for null data.
For each 16-byte record of the EHF table (+0x30 offset, +0x34 size): callback(arg, record) and record+0xc = next tmf byte (0 without tmf). Returns 1.

column2: void field_3d_pose_nodes(float frame, void *tmt, void *tms, void *world, void *hook)
column3: Poses the node tree of a TGMS at frame of a TGMT: iterative walk from TGMS +0x40 over the hierarchy table TGMS +0x18 (8 bytes per node: parent, first child, next sibling, 0xffff = none), going to the first child, else the next sibling, else climbing parents to the next unvisited sibling. Per node the TGMT node record (TGMT +0x04, 8 bytes: translation, rotation and scale track indices, 0xffff = none) gives: translation from three scalar tracks (TGMT +0x08 + index x 8, field_3d_sample_scalar_track) placed in an identity matrix and world = parent x T (the parent is identity for roots and when TGMT +0x34 bit 1 is set; without translation world = parent); rotation from field_3d_sample_rotation_track (TGMT +0x10) turned into a matrix (system_vfpu_matrix_mogrify) and multiplied in; scale from three scalar tracks applied to the three matrix rows (system_vfpu_vscl_t). Then hook +4 (node, matrix, hook) when set. world receives 64 bytes per node. VFPU code read from the Ghidra pseudo-ops; lower confidence. Returns nothing. Side effects: the world matrices. Callers: 1 (field_3d_update_model).

column2: void field_3d_pose_nodes_blend(float frame, float prev_frame, float weight, void *tmt, void *tms, void *world, void *prev_tmt, void *hook)
column3: Cross-fade variant of field_3d_pose_nodes: same node walk over TGMS +0x40/+0x18, but every channel is sampled from two animations, tmt at frame and prev_tmt at prev_frame (node records +0x04, scalar tracks +0x08, rotation tracks +0x10 of each), and blended by weight: translations and scales with system_vfpu_vector4_lerp_xyz, rotations with system_quat_slerp (identity quaternion where a node has no rotation track); world = parent x T x R x S per node (parent identity for roots and when tmt +0x34 bit 1 is set), then hook +4 (node, matrix, hook) when set. The previous animation's translation and scale track indices are used whenever the current one has the channel, without checking them for 0xffff. VFPU code read from the Ghidra pseudo-ops; lower confidence. Returns nothing. Side effects: the world matrices (64 bytes per node). Callers: 1 (field_3d_update_model).

column2: float field_3d_eval_bezier(float v0, float h1, float h2, float v1, float u)
column3: Cubic Bezier: (1-u)^3 v0 + 3(1-u)^2 u h1 + 3(1-u) u^2 h2 + u^3 v1. Returns the value. No side effects. No direct caller (the scalar segment evaluator inlines the same formula).

column2: void field_3d_sample_rotation_track(float frame, float *out, void *tmt, int *track)
column3: Samples a quaternion track of a TGMT (track = {key count, first key index}; key frames u32 at tmt +0x14, f32 quaternions of 16 bytes at tmt +0x18). Returns the handle, or 0 (0x08dd3120 = 0x80 for an invalid id). Side effects: those of audio_start_sound. Callers: 1 (audio_run_sound_script).

column2: void audio_fader16_set_target(short *fader, short target, int time)
column3: Starts a 16-bit fader move: s16 +0 = target, step s16 +6 = 0, remaining ticks s16 +8 = time x 10 / 58 for a positive time (milliseconds), -time otherwise (ticks given directly). The current value is s16 +2 with a 6-bit fraction in byte +4. Side effects: writes the fader. Callers: 5 (audio_set_sound_fader, audio_set_master_volume, audio_update_bgm_ducking, audio_update_sound_notes, ...).

column2: void audio_set_sound_fader(void *obj, int fader, short target, int time)
column3: Moves fader fader (10 bytes at obj +0x50 + fader x 10: 0 category volume, 1 fade-out, 2 pause fade, 3 volume, 4, 5 secondary/3D volume, 6 pan, 7 pitch) to target over time (audio_fader16_set_target) and sets the fader-dirty bit 0x200 of flags +0x28. Side effects: writes the fader and flags. Callers: 9 (audio_set_category_volume, audio_set_sound_volume, audio_update_frame, audio_update_sound_3d, ...).

Advances a 16-bit fader by one tick: returns 0 when the current value (+2) already equals the target (+0) and no ticks remain (+8); with zero ticks left jumps to the target (audio_fader16_init) and returns 1; otherwise computes the step (+6) on the first tick as (target x 64 - current x 64 with fraction) / ticks (at least 1), adds it with 6-bit fraction (+4), decrements the ticks and snaps to the target when it overshoots or the ticks run out. Returns 1 while it moved. Side effects: writes the fader. Callers: 2 (audio_mixer_thread, audio_update_sound_notes).

Advances an 8-bit fader by one tick, same algorithm as audio_fader16_step on the byte layout: target byte +0, current byte +1, 6-bit fraction byte +2, step s16 +4, remaining ticks s16 +6 (jumps to the target via audio_fader8_init when no ticks remain). Returns 0 when idle, 1 when it moved. Side effects: writes the fader. Callers: 2 (audio_apply_output_effect, audio_mixer_thread).

column2: void audio_compute_effect_send(void *obj, int level, short *out, uint flags)
column3: Computes the reverb send pair of a sound: unless flags bit 0x80, starts from level x the reverb volumes 0x08dd312c (left) and 0x08dd312a (right) >> 12; unless flags bit 0, adds the object's own send (u16 +0xb2 x level >> 12) panned by byte +0xac (0..0x80 after x 0x205 >> 9) with a squared loudness curve ((x >> 1) + (x^2 >> 11)) >> 1 (linear above 0x400). Stores the two results clamped to -0x1000..0x1000 in out[0], out[1]. No return value. Side effects: writes out. Callers: 1 (audio_update_sas_voice_params).

Advances the sound random generator (two words 0x08dce5c4/0x08dce5c8, seeded with 0x55555555 by audio_init): shifts the pair by one bit, XORs the first word with itself << 12 and then >> 20, and returns the new first word. Side effects: writes the generator state. Callers: 1 (audio_random_below).

Returns a random integer in 0 .. range-1 as ((audio_random_next() & 0xffff) x range) >> 16, or 0 when range < 2. Side effects: advances the generator. Callers: 4 (audio_start_sound, audio_roll_sound_variation, audio_compute_sound_note, audio_key_on_sas_voice).

column2: void audio_fader8_set_target(char *fader, char target, int time)
column3: Starts an 8-bit fader move: byte +0 = target, step s16 +4 = 0, remaining ticks s16 +6 = time x 10 / 58 for a positive time (milliseconds), -time for a negative time, 0 for 0. Side effects: writes the fader. Callers: 2 (audio_set_stream_fader_target, audio_set_output_effect).

Computes the linear volume of a sound object: the cue volume s16 +0xa0 x 0x1021 >> 7, scaled for BGM (key bit 0x100000 clear) by the current duck fader value 0x08dce616, then multiplied (>> 12 each) by the current values of faders 0-5 (+0x52, +0x5c, +0x66, +0x70, +0x7a, +0x84). With curve non-zero applies the squared loudness curve ((x >> 1) + (x^2 >> 11)) >> 1 (linear above 0x400). Returns the volume (0x1000 = full). No side effects. Callers: 1 (audio_mixer_thread).

column2: void audio_compute_pan_volumes(void *obj, int volume, int pan_base, int pan_offset, short *out, short *send_out)
column3: Turns a volume and pan into left/right levels: volume x 0x20 x s16 obj +0xa2 >> 12; pan = pan_base (0..0x7f scaled by 0x40a0 >> 14) moved by pan_offset (scaled the same) + fader 6 current (+0x8e, x 0x205 >> 9) - 0x80, clamped to 0..0x80 with 0x40 = centre; applies the squared loudness curve per side and writes out[0] (left) and out[1] (right); when send_out is given, also writes the cross-feed amounts for strongly panned sounds (else 0). No return value. Side effects: writes out and send_out. Callers: 2 (audio_update_sas_voice_params, audio_mixer_thread).

Reads a variable-length number from a sound sequence (7 bits per byte, high bit = more bytes follow, as in MIDI files) at cursor[0] + u16 position cursor+4, and advances the position past it. Returns the value. Side effects: writes the u16 position. Callers: 1 (audio_update_sound_notes).

column2: int audio_find_free_sas_voice(void *obj, int layer_tag, int exclude)
column3: Chooses a sceSas voice for obj: first reuses a voice already owned by obj (record word +0 at 0x08dce65c + v x 0x18) with the same tag byte +6, not exclude and not released (flag bit 0x04); else the lowest free voice of the allocation mask 0x08dce658 other than exclude; else steals among voices whose owner priority (+0x20e) is not above obj's: obj's own oldest voice (lowest serial u16 +8) first, otherwise the globally oldest unless obj's attribute byte 0 has bit 0x80. Returns the voice 0-31, or -1. No side effects. Callers: 2 (audio_key_on_sas_voice, audio_sas_voice_thread).

Releases a SAS voice with a short release unless its record flag (byte 0x08dce660 + voice x 0x18) has bit 0x04: resumes it (audio_sas_set_voice_pause(voice, 0)), switches to simple ADSR (0, 3) when the stored release rate byte +0x0a is above 3, keys it off and sets flag bits 0x0c. Side effects: SAS voice state, the record flag. No direct caller (reached through a function pointer or unused).

When flag bit 0x08 of the SAS voice record (byte 0x08dce660 + voice x 0x18) is clear, resumes the voice (audio_sas_set_voice_pause(voice, 0)), keys it off (audio_sas_set_key_off) and sets bit 0x08. Side effects: SAS key-off, the record flag. Callers: 2 (audio_mixer_thread, audio_update_sound_notes).

Frees the SAS voices of voice_mask: clears them in the allocation mask 0x08dce658 and, for each, when hard is non-zero and the voice has an owner, sets an instant release (audio_sas_set_adsr(voice, 8, 0x7fffffff x 4) and audio_sas_set_adsr_mode(voice, 8, 1, 1, 1, 1)), resumes it, keys it off and clears the record's owner word +0 and flag byte +4. Side effects: SAS voices, mask and records 0x08dce65c. Callers: 3 (audio_release_sas_voice, audio_release_sas_voices_locked, audio_mixer_thread).

Calls audio_release_sas_voices(voice_mask, hard) while holding the sequencer semaphore 0x08dce648 (SndSeqSema). Side effects: those of audio_release_sas_voices. No direct caller (reached through a function pointer or unused).

Waits on the sequencer semaphore 0x08dce648 and releases voice with audio_release_sas_voice; the decompiled body does not signal the semaphore again. Side effects: those of audio_release_sas_voice, semaphore count. No direct caller (reached through a function pointer or unused).

Draws the per-instance random offsets of a SAS sound from signed min/max byte pairs of its 32-byte cue: +0x14/+0x15 into obj byte +0xb0 (note transpose), +0x16/+0x17 into +0xaf (fine pitch), +0x12/+0x13 into +0xae (volume offset); each is min + audio_random_below(max - min + 1), clamped to 0..0x7f, or 0 when min == max or the result is negative. Does nothing when the cue or bank is missing. Side effects: writes those bytes. Callers: 2 (audio_sas_voice_thread, audio_update_sound_notes).

Converts a note in 1/128 semitone units to a sceSas pitch factor: semitone table u16 0x08916c70[note >> 7] interpolated toward the next entry by the fine table u16 0x08916b70[note & 0x7f] (offset from 0x1000, >> 12); clamped to 0..0xffff. Returns the pitch (0x1000 = unchanged at the root note). No side effects. Callers: 2 (audio_key_on_sas_voice, audio_update_sound_notes).

column2: int audio_compute_sound_note(void *obj, int note, int layer)
column3: Computes the pitch note (1/128 semitone units) of a layer of obj's cue: envelope record of the layer (audio_get_cue_layer_entry, audio_get_layer_envelope); note < 0 means the record's root note (byte +0x0d); base = (obj byte +0xb0 + envelope s8 +0x0c + note + 60 - root) x 128 + obj byte +0xaf, plus a random semitone from the envelope range +0x12..+0x13 and a random fine offset from +0x14..+0x15. Returns it clamped to 0x80..0x3f80, or -1 when the cue or bank is missing. Side effects: advances the random generator. Callers: 2 (audio_key_on_sas_voice, audio_update_sound_notes).

column2: int audio_key_on_sas_voice(void *obj, int layer, int note, uchar velocity, void *track, int tag)
column3: Sets up a sceSas voice for one PS-ADPCM layer of obj's cue: picks a voice (audio_find_free_sas_voice(obj, tag, -1), releasing it when owned), marks it in the mask 0x08dce658 and fills its 24-byte record at 0x08dce65c (owner, flag 0, voice, tag +6, velocity +7, serial +8 from the counter 0x08dc1a48, sample pitch u16 +0x0c from the sample header); calls audio_sas_set_voice(voice, sample data +8, sample length word +0, loop = envelope byte +8 bit 0); computes the note (audio_compute_sound_note; with a sequence track and a portamento time, glides the track's pitch fader +0x18 from the previous note) and stores audio_note_to_sas_pitch of it in +0x10; sets obj +0xac = 0x40 and the effect send +0xb2 = envelope byte +9 x 0x1021 >> 7, zero volume, the simple ADSR from envelope u16 +4/+6 (masked and ORed by the track's +0x10..+0x16 words) with the release rate kept in +0x0a, envelope volume/pan bytes +0/+1 in +0x14/+0x16, and +0x12 = 0x1000, +0x15 = 0x7f, +0x17 = 0x40 (or the track's values), plus a random volume from cue bytes +0x12/+0x13. Returns the voice, or -1 when the cue/bank is missing or no voice is free. Side effects: SAS voice set-up, voice records. Callers: 2 (audio_sas_voice_thread, audio_update_sound_notes).

Sequencer step of a type-0 sound (a note sequence on SAS voices): on the first call initialises six 0x2c-byte track states at obj +0xbc and the note slots +0x1c4, rolls the variation and reads the sequence at audio_get_cue_data_pointer + 8 (a first byte 0x80 announces byte +9 tracks with 3-byte entries holding u16 offsets; otherwise one track), setting the active-track mask +0xb8; the tick increment (float +0xb4) starts from the constant at 0x0889e5a4. Each call counts down the note durations of the slots (keying off ended notes, audio_sas_key_off_voice_once) and, for each active track whose wait expired, runs events: bytes below 0x80 are notes (velocity and duration as variable-length numbers, keyed on with audio_key_on_sas_voice into a free note slot), 0x82 call / 0x83 jump / 0x8e return (u16 offsets), 0x88 end of track (releases its voices, sets its bit in +0xb9), 0x89 wait (variable length), 0x8a layer, 0x8b volume, 0x8c pan, 0x8d pitch bend (using the bend range of 0x8f), 0x94 tempo (+0xb4 = value / constant), 0x95/0x96 ADSR1/ADSR2 AND/OR masks, 0x98 ignored byte, 0x99 portamento time, 0x9a portamento target note, 0x9b legato flag; pitch glides step the track fader (audio_fader16_step, audio_set_note_voice_param). Opcode meanings beyond the stored fields are inferred (hypothesis, confidence medium). Side effects: track and slot state, SAS voices. Callers: 1 (audio_sas_voice_thread).

Body of the thread snd_thread_seq (created by audio_init): loops waiting for bit 1 of the event flag 0x08dd31d0 (sceKernelWaitEventFlagCB, clear on exit), then under the sequencer semaphore 0x08dce648: for every one-shot ADPCM object of the list 0x08dce5fc (types 2-3) that is not paused (flags bit 0x10) and not yet keyed (+0xad bit 0x40), rolls the variation, and when enough voices are free (audio_find_free_sas_voice) keys on layer 0 and, when attribute mode is 2 (attribute byte 0 bit 0x40), layer 1 (audio_key_on_sas_voice), ORing each voice into the keyed mask +0xa8 and setting +0xad bit 0x40; started objects (bit 0x4000) count grains in +0x24. Then runs audio_update_sound_notes for the started, unpaused sequence objects of the list 0x08dce5e4 (type 0, not type 1), resetting the voice serial 0x08dc1a48 when that list is empty. Afterwards increments 0x08dc1a44 and sets bit 0x80 of the event flag. Never returns. Side effects: as described. No direct caller (thread entry started by audio_init).

Re-synchronises playing stream objects (list 0x08dce5f0, types 4-5) to a 60 Hz frame: for each, elapsed = frame x 1000 / 60 - sync frame (audio_get_stream_sync_frame) x 1000 / 60 milliseconds; when not negative seeks it (audio_seek_stream_sample) to elapsed x 441 / 10 samples (44.1 kHz) + the offset +0xec. Returns 1. Side effects: stream positions. Callers: 1 (audio_run_sound_script).

Runs a type-1 sound script, a frame-timed event list: on the first call (state byte +0xb8 bit 0x40 clear) sets the cursor +0xa4 = cue data + 0x10 and the id base +0xa8 = bank first id - u16 at cue data +8. While the state has neither bit 0x01/0x02 (ended/aborted) nor 0x20 (replaced) and the next event's u16 frame is not past the current frame +0xac, executes it: 1 starts (audio_start_sound_if_loaded) or re-syncs a stream, 2 plays a sound effect (audio_play_se) or re-syncs a stream already playing, 3 plays a sound and calls the callback +0xb0 with (id, u16 argument), each with u16 sound offset, u16 fade time (frames, scaled by the speed u16 +0xb4 through audio_scale_by_q12_u16_10 and x 0x10aa >> 8 to ms), volume byte (audio_set_sound_volume_secondary) and pan byte (audio_set_sound_pan) and a sync point (audio_set_stream_sync_point); 4 stops a sound with a fade; 5 sets a sound's secondary volume over a time; 6 ends the script (bit 0x01, all volumes back to 0x7f over 200); 7 aborts (bit 0x02). When the speed differs from 0x1000 (fast playback) it lowers all volumes to 0x30 and stops non-stream sounds of cue group 0xca, and every 8th update re-syncs the streams (audio_sync_streams_to_frame); when the speed returns to 0x1000 it restores the volumes. Copies the frame to +0x24. Side effects: sounds started, stopped and re-synced, script state. Callers: 1 (audio_update_frame).

column2: int audio_stop_sound_with_groups_2(void *sound, int fade, int also_group_c9)
column3: Stops sound at once (audio_stop_sound(sound, 0)); when that succeeded, also stops with fade every sound of cue groups 0xc8 and 0xca (audio_stop_sounds_by_selector(0xfffffec8 / 0xfffffeca, fade), group = cue byte +4) and, when also_group_c9 is non-zero, of group 0xc9. Returns 1 when the sound was stopped, else 0. Side effects: those of audio_stop_sound. No direct caller (reached through a function pointer or unused).

Pushes the mix state of one SAS voice to sceSas: level = (record byte +0x15 x velocity byte +7 x envelope volume byte +0x14, each scaled 0..0x80) >> 14; left/right dry volumes and cross-feed from audio_compute_pan_volumes(obj, level, pan byte +0x16, pan byte +0x17); the reverb send from audio_compute_effect_send (flags: record flag bit 0x20 >> 5, plus 0x80 when attribute byte 3 has bit 0x20). Unless obj is paused (flags +0x28 bit 0x10) sets the voice (+5) volumes with audio_sas_set_volume(voice, left, right, send left, send right; sends clamped to +-0x1000) and its pitch with audio_sas_set_pitch(voice, audio_scale_sound_pitch(obj, ((u16 +0x10 x u16 +0x12) >> 12) x sample pitch u16 +0x0c >> 12)). No return value. Side effects: sceSas voice parameters. Callers: 1 (audio_mixer_thread).

In-place stereo effect over count interleaved s16 frames (L, R): with d(n) = L(n) - R(n) of the input, every frame gets L(n) += d(n - 2) and R(n) -= d(n - 2), each result saturated to s16 (a side signal delayed by two frames fed back into both channels: a stereo widening, hypothesis, confidence medium). The buffer is walked backwards so the delayed values are still unmodified; the first two frames use history (the clamped d of the previous buffer's last two frames) and the last two frames' d values are saved into history for the next call. No return value. Side effects: rewrites frames and history in place. Callers: 2 (audio_apply_output_effect, audio_mixer_thread).

column2: void audio_effect_average_filter(short *history, short *buffer, int frames, int width)
column3: Moving-average low-pass over frames interleaved stereo s16 frames of buffer, in place, from the last frame backward: each output frame is the sum of width consecutive input frames (reaching into the 16 frames of the previous block saved in history) divided by width; with width 0 the samples are left unchanged. Finally saves the last 16 input frames (0x40 bytes) into history. No return value. Side effects: writes buffer and history. Callers: 2 (audio_apply_output_effect, audio_mixer_thread).

Applies the global output effect (mode byte 0x08dce5cc, set by audio_set_output_effect) to a block of 256 stereo s16 frames: mode 2 (echo) adds buffer x level (byte 0x08dce5e0 scaled to 0..0x80, / 128) into the 0x3000-frame ring 0x08dce5dc at the read position u16 0x08dce5e2 + delay (byte 0x08dce5e1 scaled x 0x5e frames); mode 3 applies audio_effect_average_filter(0x08dcda8c, buffer, 0x100, width = current of the 8-bit fader 0x08dce5d0); mode 1 applies audio_effect_filter_stereo_s16(0x08dcda84, buffer, 0x100). Steps the fader 0x08dce5d0. While the echo ring exists (VPL 0x08dce5d8 >= 0) halves the ring samples at the read position, adds them to buffer (saturated), advances the read position by 0x100 frames (wrapping at 0x3000) and, once the mode is no longer 2 and that ring block was silent, deletes the VPL (0x08dce5d8 = -1). No return value. Side effects: buffer, the echo ring, those globals. Callers: 1 (audio_mixer_thread).

Body of the thread snd_thread_main (created by audio_init); never returns. Clears the echo ring 0x08dc1a84 (0xc000 bytes), the two output blocks 0x08dcdc80 (2 x 0x400 bytes, index 0x08dce480) and the six stream rings 0x08dd3200 (6 x 0x6000 bytes). Each 256-frame grain (44.1 kHz stereo s16): clears the output block; under the sound semaphore 0x08dce654 steps the duck fader 0x08dce614, counts down each object's retrigger byte +0x31, steps the 8 faders of objects with dirty faders (or BGM while ducking) and stores audio_compute_sound_volume in +0xa2; services the 32 SAS voices of started, keyed, unpaused owners: first keys them on (audio_update_sas_voice_params, audio_sas_set_key_on), later updates changed parameters, keys off voices that reached their end (audio_sas_get_end_flag) and frees keyed-off voices whose envelope fell below 0x100 (marking them in the owner's ended mask +0xa4). Wakes the sequencer thread (event flag 0x08dd31d0 bit 1). Under the ATRAC decode semaphore 0x08dce64c it orders the playing stream objects (list 0x08dce5f0) by buffered samples and, for each (slot = +0x30 - 0x1c), primes it once (sceAtracResetPlayPosition, sceAtracSetLoopNum(-1)), honours a stop request +0xe3 (sceAtracSetLoopNum 0), reads sceAtracGetLoopStatus, decodes with sceAtracDecodeData into its 0x1000-frame ring (budget 0xc00/0x800/0 frames depending on the SAS one-shot count 0x08dce604), keeps the level meter (+0xc8, mean absolute sample) when enabled, filters by stream mode +0xe2 (1 average filter, 2 stereo filter), mixes 256 frames into the block with its pan gains (copy when alone at full gain, scaled or saturating-added otherwise; skipped when attribute byte 3 has bit 0x80), handles the loop offset +0xb0 and end (pads with silence), counts grains +0x24 and sends the stream into the echo ring 0x08dc1a84 with level +0xe0 and delay +0xe1 x 0x5e frames. Then adds the decaying echo ring into the block, applies the output effect (audio_apply_output_effect) before or after the SAS mix depending on byte 0x08dce5cd (0x10 effect on SAS output first, 0x20 before, 0x30 after audio_sas_core_with_mix), outputs the block on channel 2 with audio_output_panned_blocking at the master fader level (s16 0x08dce622 x 2), swaps blocks, waits for the sequencer (event bit 0x80) and steps the master fader 0x08dce620. Exact stream ring arithmetic read from a long decompilation (confidence medium). Side effects: audio output, all mixer state. No direct caller (thread entry started by audio_init).

Clears the per-stream state of a stream object's slot (slot = signed byte +0x30 - 0x1c, 0-5): the 16 stereo history frames at 0x08dcdacc + slot x 0x40 (filter history) and the 0x6000-byte decode ring at 0x08dd3200 + slot x 0x6000 (system_memset). Side effects: writes those buffers. Callers: 1 (audio_start_atrac_voice).

newlib _open syscall over the PSP I/O manager: translates the newlib O_* flags (access mode 0/1/2 to PSP_O_RDONLY 1 / WRONLY 2 / RDWR 3, O_APPEND 0x8 to 0x100, keeps 0x200/0x400/0x800 = CREAT/TRUNC/EXCL, O_NONBLOCK 0x4000 to 0x4) and calls sceIoOpen(path, flags, 0x1a4 = mode 0644). Returns the sceIoOpen result (file descriptor or negative error) through the tail of the call. Side effects: opens a file. No direct caller (newlib syscall layer, unused by the game).

column2: int system_sys_lseek(int fd, int offset, int whence)
column3: newlib _lseek syscall: maps descriptors 0/1/2 to sceKernelStdin/Stdout/Stderr, returns 0xfffffff7 (-9) for a negative descriptor, otherwise forwards to sceIoLseek; the forwarding of offset and whence is hidden by the decompiler (passed on as the sceIoLseek offset and whence, hypothesis, confidence medium). Returns the new position or a negative error. Side effects: moves the file position. Callers: 1 (system_lseek_r).

newlib _exit: when the module reentrancy struct (system_get_module_reent) is not the calling thread's (system_get_reent) it prints a libc error with sceKernelPrintf and ends only the thread (sceKernelExitThread(status)); otherwise reclaims the reentrancy struct (system_reclaim_reent), unregisters it (system_unregister_module_reent, which returns the owning module id) and, when that module is not the current one, stops and unloads it and exits the thread; else calls sceKernelStopUnloadSelfModuleWithStatus(1, 0, 0, 0, 0). Does not return. Callers: 1 (system_exit).

Moves the break by increment when it stays inside [start, end]. Returns the old break, or 0xffffffff when the area cannot be created (size 0) or the new break would leave it. Side effects: the globals 0x08916dd0-0x08916ddc, partition allocation. Callers: 2 (system_user_main_thread, system_sbrk_r).

column3: The playback loop of system_movie_play: waits (1 ms steps, system_movie_wait_waitflag_bit1) until the reader has prefetched (system_movie_reader_is_done), then per iteration checks for the end of playback (system_movie_check_playback_end) and, once it reported 0, polls the skip buttons (system_movie_poll_skip_button; a skip flushes the decoder with sceMpegAvcDecodeFlush and returns the poll result); stops when the reader hit EOF and the ring buffer is empty again (sceMpegRingbufferAvailableSize == ring_packets x 4); decodes one audio (system_movie_decode_audio, the first call initialises) and one video access unit (system_movie_decode_video), tolerating error 0x80618001 (no AU yet); calls sceKernelCheckCallback and sceKernelPowerTick(6). After the end it drains the decoder with system_movie_stop_video. Returns 0 at a normal end, the skip result, or a negative error; abort bit 0x800 also ends the loop. Side effects: decoding into the display/audio queues. Callers: 1 (system_movie_play).

Reads the first 0x800 bytes of the movie (system_movie_reader_read_async), gets the stream offset (sceMpegQueryStreamOffset into out_offset) and size (sceMpegQueryStreamSize into out_size). Returns 0 on success, -1 on a short read or error. Side effects: reads the file. Callers: 1 (system_movie_play).

Skip check during a movie: reads the pad (sceCtrlReadBufferPositive), keeps the previous buttons in 0x08924ad0 and the current ones in 0x08924ad4. Unless movie flag bit 0x4 (0x08924ac8, skip disabled) is set, a new press of any button (flag bit 0x2), of SELECT (0x1) or of START (0x8) sets the playback state 0x08924ab8 = 10 and returns 1; otherwise returns 0. Side effects: 0x08924ad0, 0x08924ad4, 0x08924ab8. Callers: 1 (system_movie_decode_loop).

column2: int system_movie_audio_queue_create(void *queue, int frame_size, int count, void *flags, uint *alloc, int keep_channel)

On a channel error clears the tables and returns -1; returns 0 on success. Side effects: audio channel reservation, semaphore, *alloc advanced. Callers: 1 (system_movie_play).
Clears the counters 0x08924ad8 / 0x08924adc and the queue's write index (+0x0c), read index (+0x10) and count (+0x14). Returns 0. Side effects: those words. Callers: 1 (system_movie_play).

Releases the audio output channels unless keep_channel (audio_release_output_channels), deletes the semaphore (+0x00), clears the buffer and timestamp tables and the two output buffer words 0x08924ae4 / 0x08924ae8. Returns 0. Side effects: audio channels, semaphore, queue fields. Callers: 1 (system_movie_play).

Stores in *out the buffer at the write index (+0x0c) of the audio queue's buffer table (+0x04), or 0 when the queue is full (system_movie_audio_queue_get_free < 1). No return value. Side effects: writes *out. Callers: 1 (system_movie_decode_audio).

Stores the timestamp of the slot at the write index (+0x0c) in the timestamp table (+0x08); pts -1 means last timestamp (+0x24) + the step 0x08924ae0. Keeps it in +0x24. Returns 0. Side effects: queue fields. Callers: 1 (system_movie_decode_audio).
Stores the timestamp at the read index (+0x10) of the audio queue's timestamp table (+0x08) in *out. Returns 0. Side effects: writes *out. Callers: 1 (system_movie_get_av_sync_state).
Returns capacity (+0x18) - count (+0x14) of the audio queue. No side effects. Callers: 3 (system_movie_decode_audio, system_movie_audio_queue_get_write_buffer, system_movie_check_playback_end).
Returns the number of queued audio frames (+0x14). No side effects. Callers: 2 (system_movie_get_av_sync_state, system_movie_audio_thread).
True when bit 0x8 of the queue's event flag (+0x20, system_movie_get_event_flag_bits) is set. No side effects. Callers: 1 (system_movie_audio_thread).

Side effects: audio output, queue counters. No direct caller (thread entry created by system_movie_play).

Copies one decoded frame (size +0x1c) into the current output buffer (0x08924ae4 / 0x08924ae8 by the toggle 0x08924aec), advances the read index (+0x10) modulo the capacity, outputs the buffer on channel 0 with audio_output_panned_blocking at the movie volume 0x0889f678 for both sides, and toggles 0x08924aec. Returns 0. Side effects: audio output, queue read index. Callers: 1 (system_movie_audio_output_next).

column2: int system_movie_decode_audio(void *mpeg, void *ctx, void *queues, int init)
column3: When the audio queue (queues[1]) has a free slot: gets an ATRAC access unit (sceMpegGetAtracAu with ctx +0x08 / +0x0c), decodes it into the queue's write buffer (sceMpegAtracDecode, init flag), stores the AU timestamp (system_movie_audio_queue_set_write_pts) and, unless init, pushes the frame (system_movie_audio_queue_push). Returns 0, 1 when the queue is full, or the sceMpeg error. Side effects: the audio queue. Callers: 1 (system_movie_decode_loop).

When the display queue (queues[0]) has a free slot: gets an AVC access unit (sceMpegGetAvcAu with ctx +0x00 / +0x04), decodes it into the queue's write buffer (sceMpegAvcDecode, stride 0x200, buffer pointer kept in 0x08924af4), pushes the AU timestamp (system_movie_video_pts_queue_push) and, when a picture was output, pops the oldest timestamp into the display slot and pushes the frame (system_movie_display_push). Returns 0, 1 when the queue is full, or the sceMpeg error. Side effects: display and timestamp queues. Callers: 1 (system_movie_decode_loop).

Drains the decoder at the end: with a free display slot calls sceMpegAvcDecodeStop into the write buffer; when it returned a picture pops a timestamp and pushes the frame. Returns 0 when nothing more came out or a frame was pushed, 1 when the queue is full, or the sceMpeg error. Side effects: display and timestamp queues. Callers: 1 (system_movie_decode_loop).

column2: int system_movie_display_create(void *display, int frame_size, int count, void *flags, uint *alloc)

Returns the sceDisplaySetMode result (negative on failure, tables cleared). Side effects: display mode, kernel objects, *alloc. Callers: 1 (system_movie_play).

Clears the frame counters 0x08924afc / 0x08924b00 and the queue's write index (+0x10), read index (+0x14) and count (+0x18), sets state 1, clears the delay event flag, sets the display mode 480 x 272 and a null frame buffer. Returns 0 or the sceDisplaySetMode error. Side effects: queue fields, display. Callers: 1 (system_movie_play).

column3: Evaluates an EHF track at frame - placed_frame: starts from the base matrix (ui_ehf_track_base_matrix) and the identity colour transform 0x0889ee00; with keys (u16 +0x26 count, stride u16 +0x28, keys at +0x2c), holds the first key at or before it and the last key at or after it, finds an exact key by binary search, else interpolates linearly between the two surrounding keys. Builds a 4x4 row-vector matrix from an EHF track's base values (a, b, c, d, tx, ty): rows (a, b, 0, 0), (c, d, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1, 0), (tx, ty, 0, 1), i.e. x' = a*x + c*y + tx, y' = b*x + d*y + ty. Side effects: writes out_matrix. Callers: 2 (ui_ehf_draw_shape_instance_array, ui_ehf_eval_track).
